oneStopSecurity.note: FMG: depending on origin and destination, connecting passengers may have to pass security again. EU one-stop security (Reg. 2015/1998 Attachment 4-B as amended by Reg. 2019/413 and 2025/920): passengers from EU / EEA / Swiss airports and from the recognised third countries are not re-screened on transfer. Ben Gurion (TLV) was removed by Reg. 2025/920, Kangerlussuaq, Guernsey, Isle of Man and Jersey too. Belgrade (BEG) was added by Reg. 2020/111 and not removed since (consolidated text reconstructed from mirrors, likely: docs/research/EVIDENCE_2026-11-02.md); Reg. 2025/920 applies from 21 May 2025. The official consolidated Attachment 4-B was not read (EUR-Lex: owner capture).

specialScreening.text: Flights to Israel (El Al, Israir and Lufthansa "Abflüge nach Tel Aviv: T1 F") check in and depart at Terminal 1 Hall F, a separate building reachable only on foot through the public area. Connecting passengers follow "Exit / Hall F":  they leave the airside area and pass check-in and security again. Feed 2026-10-30 – 11-01: all 9 TLV departures (LH, LY, BZ) report terminal "1F". No screening duration is published.

US-bound flights: TSA / DHS enhanced security measures for all last-point-of-departure airports (2017, still the baseline as far as known) may add checks at check-in or at the gate (interviews, document checks, separate screening of electronics). The procedures are not public; no time is known.

rules.text: Terminal 2 separates Schengen and non-Schengen by level on the same stands: G (Level 04) Schengen, H (Level 05) non-Schengen, bus gates on Level 03. The satellite (airside only, no check-in or reclaim) mirrors this: K Schengen, L non-Schengen one floor up, J apron-bus gates.

The satellite is reachable only by the underground PTS people mover from the T2 main building: daily 04:00–24:00 every 4 min, about 1 min ride (measured 55–65 s), two stations ('Gates G,H' and 'Gates J,K,L'). Schengen and non-Schengen flows are separated within the trains. Between 00:00 and 04:00 the satellite is not routable.

Between Terminal 1 and Terminal 2 a free shuttle bus for connecting passengers runs in the non-public area (06:00–23:00; every 10 min 07:00–17:00, otherwise every 20 min; ride 5–7 min), with separate Schengen (T1 C08 ↔ T2 G83) and non-Schengen (T1 A28 ↔ T2 H side) stops. Walking between the terminals is possible only via the public side (MAC) with new checks and is not recommended by FMG.

Terminal 1 is built as modules A–E (E arrivals only) plus the separate Hall F; before April 2026 A and D were Schengen, B and C non-Schengen, and each module was self-contained airside. Since 21 April 2026 all T1 non-Schengen flights use the new T1 Pier (gates A40–A51, remote A60–A64). The present border zone of legacy modules A, B and C is not fully documented.

FMG: depending on origin and destination, connecting passengers may have to pass security again and must pass passport control between Schengen and non-Schengen. The T1 Pier has a transfer security checkpoint on Level 05 and a transfer border control in module B (Level 04); the satellite has transfer security lanes.
Guides report a MUC minimum connecting time of 30–45 min (30 domestic / 45 international, or 40 min overall); no official MCT table was read. Times in this model are movement-only, not MCTs.

Night (published hours): the T1–T2 transfer bus runs 06:00–23:00 and the PTS 04:00–24:00. Between 23:00 and 06:00 the model routes T1 ↔ T2 connections only via the public side (arrivals/exit, MAC, security again); between 00:00 and 04:00 the satellite (J/K/L) is unreachable. Checkpoint opening hours at night are not published and are not modelled.

Baggage: on one booking, checked bags are transferred automatically to the connecting flight (FMG); with separate bookings whose bags are not checked through, the passenger reclaims the bags, leaves through customs, re-checks them and passes security (and border control) again, so the connection is a landside self-transfer. EU law: hold baggage from a non-EU airport transferred at MUC onto an intra-EU flight is customs-controlled at the last international EU airport of arrival (or at MUC when the onward flight goes to another international German airport, a choice of the Member State that no read source settles for MUC); cabin baggage is controlled at MUC. The model has no reclaim or bag-drop step: self-transfer times exclude waiting at the belt and re-check-in.

openQuestions.question: Since the T1 Pier opened (21 Apr 2026), which border zone do legacy modules A, B and C serve, and do any T1 modules share an airside area (the 2024 video shows a long airside shopping hall after 'Departures Gates B, C, D')?
openQuestions.impact: Modules A and B are modelled as 'mixed' with no airside links; C is Schengen on one official diagram only. Routes to A/B/C gates go via the public side and may be longer than reality.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Owner capture of the official digital map (munich-airport.com airport map, Apple Maps embed) or a dated post-April-2026 walk through T1 modules A–C with readable signs.

openQuestions.question: From the Schengen transfer-bus stop at C08, can passengers reach Schengen gates in modules A, B and D airside (the official diagram labels the stop 'Terminal 1 Gates A, B, C, D')?
openQuestions.impact: Schengen T2 → T1 D/A transfers currently route via the public side with security.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Recent transfer video T2 G83 → T1, or FMG transfer-desk confirmation.

openQuestions.question: Where exactly is the non-Schengen transfer-bus stop in T2 (gate number on the H side), and do passengers arriving by bus pass a transfer security check?
openQuestions.impact: Stop placement and access minutes are assumed.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Post-pier ride video A28 → T2, or the official map.

openQuestions.question: How does a passenger arriving at the T1 Pier (non-Schengen) connect to a T1 Schengen gate: via the transfer border control in module B (Level 04), and is security repeated?
openQuestions.impact: Pier → C/D currently routes through the public side (entry passport, then module security).
openQuestions.howToResolve: Pocket-guide flow confirmation or a dated transfer video.

openQuestions.question: Which PTS cars/platforms serve non-Schengen arrivals versus departures (the 2016 report mentions a fourth car for a third flow), and where do L arrivals clear entry passport control?
openQuestions.impact: Non-Schengen PTS line confidence is probable; L → T2 exit routes via K (entry passport) and the Schengen cars.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Full read of the Business Traveller article (HTTP 403 to automated fetch) or a dated L-arrival video.

openQuestions.question: Is Hall F in use in autumn 2026, which gate numbers does it use, and for which flights?
openQuestions.impact: Hall F has no gates and is outside the matrix.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Official map capture or a dated photo of Hall F signage.

openQuestions.question: How do connecting passengers move between T1 and T2 when the transfer bus does not run (23:00–06:00)?
openQuestions.impact: With a time of 23:00–06:00 the model routes T1 ↔ T2 connections via the public side (passport/security again); whether an on-demand airside transfer exists and whether the T2 central checkpoint and the T1 Level 05 checkpoints are open then is unknown.
openQuestions.howToResolve: FMG transfer-desk or ground-handling statement; checkpoint opening hours (not on the official security page, re-read 2026-10-31). The FMG PDF "openinghours security checkpoints 01062025" lists STAFF screening points only (T1 Modul A and C closed, Modul D 03:30–21:30, Modul C crew 24 h); it does not give passenger checkpoint hours and is not used as passenger evidence.

openQuestions.question: Unattested gate numbers: A13, B01/B03/B04/B13, C02, D02/D05/D08/D13/D18/D19/D22, G71/G73–G80, K02/K17/K29, L10/L12/L14/L16–L18/L20/L29; and the zone of J01–J06.

Do legacy modules A and B still have their own departure security checkpoints after the pier opened, or are Schengen passengers for A/B gates screened at the module C/D Level 5 checkpoints and then walk airside?
openQuestions.impact: Routes to modules A and B (and the 52 inferred matrix cells) use a module checkpoint that may not exist; real routes may be shorter (via C/D) or impossible (A/B used only for non-Schengen bus boarding).
openQuestions.howToResolve: Owner capture of the official digital map (Apple Maps embed) or a dated post-April-2026 departure walk to an A or B gate.

openQuestions.question: Where did the replacement buses of the 2024 PTS suspension board and alight (G/H bus gates? J gates?), and were Schengen and non-Schengen passengers carried separately?
openQuestions.impact: Historical only; the replacement bus is not modelled, so routes to the satellite are unroutable on dates inside a PTS suspension.
openQuestions.howToResolve: FMG statement or archived X post; repeat if another suspension is announced.

openQuestions.question: Non-Schengen arrival at MUC connecting to a German domestic flight on one ticket: are the checked bags customs-controlled at MUC (EU 2015/2447 Art. 39(2) allows the transfer airport when the onward flight goes to another international airport of the same Member State) or at the destination airport?
openQuestions.impact: If Germany applies the control at MUC, such passengers would reclaim their bags at MUC and the airside connection modelled today would be wrong for them. No read source states it; the model assumes bags are checked through (FMG transfer page).
openQuestions.howToResolve: Lufthansa connection pages (lufthansa.com answered HTTP 403: owner capture) or a zoll.de/FMG statement on international-to-domestic transfers.

openQuestions.question: How long do baggage reclaim and re-check-in take for a self-transfer at MUC (T1 pier belts B1–B4, T2 belts)?
openQuestions.impact: Self-transfer routes go landside through the arrivals exit and departure security, but the reclaim wait and bag drop are not in the model (no schema field), so these routes are too short.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Schema: a reclaim/bag-drop step or profile flag; data: FMG or uncut video timing.
